newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Ex Venezuelan official calls for early election.
newsitem.headline: Ex Venezuelan official calls for early election.

text.p: Former Venezuelan Attorney General Jesus Petit Da Costa called on Friday for presidential elections to be brought forward to avoid a political crisis in the event of President Rafael Caldera's death.
It was the first time a leading political figure had spoken publicly of the possibility that the 81-year-old president might not complete his five year term.
"The country needs a strong government...We cannot wait until February 1999," Da Costa told a news conference.
Da Costa, who resigned as attorney general in February citing differences with members of Caldera's cabinet of ministers, said the president's age meant he should step down.
"President Caldera is not in condition to give the country the government it needs in the present circumstances."
As well as "a state of health which creates insuperable physical limitations," Caldera's popularity has plummeted and his fragile support in Congress has disintegrated, Da Costa said.

Stuttering economic growth and Latin America's highest inflation rates have seen Caldera's popularity rating drop from over 70 percent when he started his second term in February 1994 to under 30 percent in the latest opinion polls.

Once an energetic and rousing speaker, Caldera has appeared increasing frail and stiff in recent months creating feverish speculation about his health. Government officials insist the president could not be fitter.
Da Costa proposed bringing forward presidential elections from Dec. 1998 to later this year to name a successor who could take over should Caldera die or decide to resign.
"I'm not proposing that President Caldera quits, what I'm proposing is simply that we elect his successor in advance," he said.
There was no immediate reaction from the president's office.
